 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. UFC Qatar is set to deliver one of the year's low-key best fight nights — or days, depending on where you are in the world.
 In the perpetually cursed light heavyweight division, the title picture has stalled since champion Carlos Ulberg tore his ACL in his title win in April. Coincidentally, to win that title, Ulberg knocked out ex-champ Jiří Procházka, who is back for Saturday's UFC Qatar headliner. Standing in his way will be rising young contender Navajo Stirling, who has been a brute force in his undefeated 11-fight career.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The co-main event also carries high stakes, as Aljamain Sterling and Kevin Vallejos aim to make their case for the next featherweight title shot. Overall, UFC Qatar feels like a throwback to the types of fight nights we used to get during the Fox era. If you know, you know.
 👑 UFC Qatar's lineup Crown grade: A 👑 
 Will "Dad Jiří" become the latest mythical MMA fighter?
 (Ed Mulholland via Getty Images) 205 pounds: Jiří Procházka (+130) vs. Navajo Stirling (-155)
 Anyone who's watched any Procházka fight knows the man is mandatory viewing.
 Arguably the most get-or-get-got fighter in MMA history, it's impossible not to be excited for any Procházka event. The story ahead of this fight centers around his efforts to rebound from that devastating Ulberg loss while becoming a father in the meantime. Since his 2024 loss to former champion Alex Pereira, Prochazka has shown obvious improvements in his defensive game, but maintained his patented unorthodox style akin to a "Blade Runner" version of Keith Jardine. Essentially, I'm calling the man a "Herky Jerky" cyberpunk android, and that's the greatest compliment I can think of.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement In the infamous words of former NFL head coach Raheem Morris, Stirling is the latest and greatest "yungry" rising superstar at light heavyweight. (That means young and hungry, if you couldn't figure that out.) A Contender Series alum out of City Kickboxing, Stirling has a perfectly massive build for the 205-pound division and utilizes his length very well. He's an intimidating presence who can match the physical elements Procházka also possesses. We knew he had power, but cracking the chin of always-durable former champion Jan Blachowicz last time out really proved it.
 I've said it once, probably more, throughout our Uncrowned previews, but I can never pick against Procházka — unless he's going against a dominant wrestler who just doesn't exist in the current light heavyweight landscape. This is not one of those cases, and it admittedly feels like a make-or-break point for Procházka and whether he'll stick around at the top of division in 2027. His dangerous striking hasn't gone anywhere, but his chin is starting to let him down more often than he'd like.
 Procházka isn't necessarily a slow starter. He's best, however, when he slowly drags opponents into chaos after Round 1. So, that first round will be critical for Stirling, and if he doesn't spark Procházka, he'll need to avoid the imminent war, which seems like too big of an ask that he hasn't had to deal with yet.
 Pick: Procházka 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement 145 pounds: Aljamain Sterling (+115) vs. Kevin Vallejos (-135)
 Sound the alarms. We have Stirling and Sterling on the same card, ladies and gentlemen.
 With this Sterling, we know what we're getting at this stage. The former UFC bantamweight champion is as strong of a grappler as the featherweight division possesses. A human weighted blanket, Sterling accompanies his game with a consistent and versatile kicking game that dares his opponents to counter with takedowns.
 Vallejos, 24, is the future of featherweight. He's far exceeded expectations for his youth, scoring very impressive knockouts of Josh Emmett and Giga Chikadze in his past two Octagon appearances. He's a wildly dangerous striker who chains together great variety in his combinations.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement There's a problem here with his matchup, though. Not for Sterling, but for Vallejos, who lacks experience against a wrestler anywhere near the former champ's caliber. Sterling is defensively sound enough to get past anything Vallejos offers, and his takedown threats alone will negate Vallejos' offense.
 Pick: Sterling 
 155 pounds: Dan Hooker (-185) vs. Brian Ortega (+155)
 Oddly enough, there was a time when Dan Hooker vs. Brian Ortega could have happened as a back-end featherweight top-15 clash.
 Hooker is making a very quick turnaround after last competing against Salahdine Parnasse in September. That trip to enemy territory didn't go "Hangman's" way, extending his losing streak to three. In his losses, though, he's stayed dangerous, as always, with his strong, whipping kickboxing game. He just hasn't been fighting slouches by any means.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement It's difficult to know what type of Brian Ortega we'll get at this stage. Admittedly, "T-City" feels like a complete afterthought after fading out of the featherweight ranks and failing to make weight in his last appearance, a lopsided five-round decision loss to Sterling. Ortega simply doesn't seem motivated to fight anymore, and that's incredibly dangerous against someone like Hooker.
 Ortega is always a submission threat, no matter how badly he gets smacked around the cage. He's almost too tough for his own good. So, expect this fight to look like either of Ortega's last two fights, with him getting beat on until the brink of collapse.
 Pick: Hooker 
 Kyoji Horiguchi is ready to rebound.
 (Chris Unger via Getty Images) 125 pounds: Kyoji Horiguchi (-200) vs. Asu Almabayev (+165)
 Somewhere, Manel Kape is smiling, knowing his "children" are going at it this weekend.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Kyoji Horiguchi and Asu Almabayev both last tasted defeat against Kape. For Horiguchi, that was in June, while Almabayev has won three straight since his March 2025 meeting with Kape.
 Unlike Almabayev, Horiguchi found his usual success against Kape, moving laterally and dicing up Kape until the division's next title challenger landed a nuke-like fist to the face. That's been Horiguchi's biggest problem since he evolved in his initial post-UFC run from 2017 onward: He's taking big shots worse and worse.
 Luckily for Horiguchi, Almabayev has never been a noteworthy knockout artist at 125 pounds, leaning much more on his great grappling ability. He has three knockout wins compared to 11 submission wins, and will do his best to track down and get ahold of the former two-division RIZIN champion.
 Still, Horiguchi's wrestling game has come a long way, thanks to his work at American Top Team. This should be his fight to lose.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Pick: Horiguchi 
 185 pounds: Jared Cannonier (+245) vs. Ikram Aliskerov (-305)
 Jared Cannonier is out here still shooting for the stars. Good on him. Is he well past his expiration date? It sure seems that way after lopsided performances against Michael Page and Christian Leroy Duncan. But a few things remain true about Cannonier: He packs power and can absorb more damage than his brain surely prefers.
 Ikram Aliskerov has been the total package with plenty of hype around him since he entered the UFC in 2023. His literal only kryptonite, somewhat comically, has been uppercuts, which resulted in losses to former middleweight champions Robert Whittaker and Khamzat Chimaev.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Everything Aliskerov does is heavy and concise. Expect him to land damage aplenty on Cannonier while wearing him down against the cage or mat if necessary. At range, he'll land at a higher clip. Everything about this matchup says the UFC sees Cannonier as a gatekeeper, if his last outing didn't already show it.
 Pick: Aliskerov 
 Preliminary Notes
 Jake Matthews has to be one of UFC's all-time prelim GOATs. I mean, think about how many fights the still relatively young veteran has under his belt and where they've mostly taken place. It feels like a prelim-or-fight-night career, but he's made it this far, so kudos to the Aussie stalwart.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Elsewhere, Alexandre Topuria is back in action, while a compelling flyweight contender affair pits Amir Albazi against Alessandro Costa in a battle for rankings supremacy.
 UFC Qatar is good, folks. Embrace it.
